## Purpose

This crate is one deterministic miner cut into one module per pipeline stage — ingest, extract, graph, mine/dictionary, condense — then the projections (`digest`, `facts`, `spec`, `rank`, `pagerank`). `main.rs` declares every module in a single `mod` block and `analyze()` is the only place the stages are chained, so a module is a stage or a projection, never a service object with a lifecycle. A module knows the *engine*; the vocabulary it operates on (languages, build systems, tool markers, stopwords, tuning constants) lives in sibling `.toml` files or in `build.rs`-generated `OUT_DIR` code, so extending coverage is a data row rather than a branch. The product is `grain.model.json`: projections read the finished `ProjectModel` and never re-walk the repository. Output has to be byte-identical across runs and machines, which is why the modules reach for `BTreeMap`/`BTreeSet`, explicit sorts with tie-breakers, and fixed-point `_x1024` integers instead of floats.

## Convention

Folder: apps/scan/src/** · Extension: .rs · Files of this role in this subproject: 17

- **Header.** Each module read here opens with a `//!` block that names its layer/stage and — just as important — states what it must never learn: `extract.rs` lists the whole generic capture vocabulary and says "nothing language-specific lives in this file"; `classify.rs` says every tool name lives in the catalog; `dictionary.rs` argues why it is a scan stage and not a projection.
- **Public surface.** A handful of free functions carrying the stage's verb (`ingest`, `classify`, `build`, `build_skeleton`, `query`, `mine`, `rank`, `compile`), placed right after the module's consts and types, with private helpers below them in call order. `impl` blocks are rare and small (`Overrides::load` in `classify.rs`); there are no traits, builders or dependency-injected services.
- **Visibility.** `pub` for what `main.rs` or another stage calls; `pub(crate)` for internals shared sideways (`digest::stopwords`, `digest::tokenize`, `facts::owned_manifests`, `ingest::under_test_dir`, `matching::fold`). A consumer calls the owner module-qualified — `classify.rs` states outright that the digest uses `crate::classify::…` instead of a local wrapper.
- **Types.** Model types (`model.rs`) are plain structs with public fields deriving `Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Debug, Default`, usually with `#[serde(default)]` on the struct; a field added later carries `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "…")]` so older payloads keep deserialising and the common case stays off the wire (`Module::file_class`, `Module::fan_in`). Projection structs (`digest.rs`) are `pub(crate)` and derive `Serialize` only.
- **Data over literals.** Six modules embed a sibling table with `include_str!("../<name>.toml")` (`classify`, `digest`, `rank`, `manifests`, `ingest`, `stemmers`) and parse it once behind a function-local `static X: OnceLock<T>` accessor; `extract.rs` gets its grammar registry only through `include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), …))`. Caps and thresholds are named `const` at the top of the module (`MAX_TERMS`, `MIN_COUNT`, `Q_MAX_FILES`), never inline numbers.
- **Failure style.** `anyhow::Result` appears only at the IO boundary (`ingest::ingest`, `main`); stages return their value and degrade instead of aborting — `Option` for "no verdict" (`classify::classify`), `.ok().and_then(…).unwrap_or_default()` for an unreadable sidecar, an individually discarded row for a catalog regex that will not compile, a skipped language for a grammar that will not load. `expect` shows up only on an embedded table (a programmer error caught by any test run).
- **Tests.** Ten of the seventeen modules end with an inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { use super::*; }` that exercises the *generic* engine with invented extensions and fake vocabulary; assertions that name a real ecosystem, marker or grammar live outside `src/` in `apps/scan/tests/*.rs` — `classify.rs` writes that split down as a comment above its test module.

## How to apply

A new stage or projection is a new file `apps/scan/src/<stage>.rs` with one responsibility, a `//!` header stating its layer and its blind spots, and a `mod <stage>;` line in the block at the top of `main.rs` (keep it beside its alphabetical neighbours). Decide first *where it runs*: if it needs the in-memory `content` map (comments, raw source) it is a scan-time stage wired into `analyze()` next to `mine`/`dictionary`; if the finished model is enough, it is a projection taking `&ProjectModel` and returning a `Serialize` struct, like `digest`/`facts`. Give it one `pub fn` entry point named for the stage and keep the helpers private below it. If it needs a CLI face, add a variant to the `Command` enum in `main.rs` — the doc comment *is* the help text, `path: PathBuf` comes first, tuning knobs are `#[arg(long, default_value…)]`, `out: Option<PathBuf>` comes last — plus the match arm that pretty-prints JSON to `out` or stdout. Anything naming a language, extension, build system, tool or grammar node goes into a sibling `.toml` read through a `OnceLock` accessor, never into a `match` in your module. When you extend `ProjectModel`, add the field with `#[serde(default)]` so old models still load. Iterate ordered collections and finish with an explicit sort plus a tie-breaker before truncating, so two runs serialize the same bytes.
